{{nihongo|'''Yashirogi Shrine'''|矢代寸神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

'''Yashirogi Shrine''' (やしろぎじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located at 357 Hatta-chō, {{ill|Kishiwada, Osaka|ar|كيشيوادا (أوساكا)|arz|كيشيوادا, اوساكا|be|Кісівада|ca|Kishiwada|ce|Кисивада|ceb|Kishiwada Shi|de|Kishiwada|eo|Kishiwada|es|Kishiwada|eu|Kishiwada (Osaka)|fa|کیشی‌وادا، اوساکا|fi|Kishiwada|fr|Kishiwada|ga|Kishiwada|gl|Kishiwada|hr|Kishiwada|hy|Կիսիվադա|id|Kishiwada, Osaka|it|Kishiwada|ja|岸和田市|ko|기시와다시|lt|Kišivada|mg|Kishiwada|mzn|کیشی‌وادا، اوساکا|nl|Kishiwada|no|Kishiwada|pl|Kishiwada|pt|Kishiwada|ro|Kishiwada|ru|Кисивада|sh|Kishivada|simple|Kishiwada, Osaka|sr|Кишивада|sv|Kishiwada|tg|Кишиуада|th|คิชิวาดะ|tl|Kishiwada|tr|Kishiwada|tt|Кисивада|uk|Кішівада|ur|کیشیوادا، اوساکا|vi|Kishiwada, Ōsaka|war|Kishiwada, Osaka|zh|岸和田市|zh_classical|岸和田市|zh_min_nan|Kisiwada-chhī|zh_yue|岸和田|qid=Q740456}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it is listed as the Yashiro Village Shrine of Junior Fifth Rank, and the area was formerly called Yashiro Village (Yashirogi). The record states that Yashirogi Shrine was enshrined here, with one seat being the main shrine, known as Ichinomiya, located in the present-day Ōaza Hatta, aza Miyauchi, and another seat known as Suwa Shrine or Yashirogi Lower Shrine, which was located in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamisuyachō}} of the same city. During the Edo period, it served as the Ichinomiya of the {{ill|Kishiwada Domain|fr|Domaine de Kishiwada|ja|岸和田藩|ko|기시와다번|zh|岸和田藩|qid=Q3034469}}, and when the domain lord changed, it was customary to pay respects at all shrines within the domain; later, this was limited to worship at this shrine alone. Although it is a shrine with a long history, it currently has no resident priest, and is administered concurrently by the chief priest (the Sakai family) of the nearby {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Habiki Shrine}}.

=== History ===
* {{ill|503|Q30975|qid=Q30975}} (Year 1 of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|Q349277|qid=Q349277}}): The shrine is established.
* {{ill|1090|Q19466|qid=Q19466}} (Kanji 4): In January, {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|Q60949|qid=Q60949|lt=Retired Emperor Shirakawa}} visits the shrine during his {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumano pilgrimage}}.
* {{ill|1640|Q6901|qid=Q6901}} (Kan’ei 17): {{ill|Okabe Nobukatsu|Q11473826|qid=Q11473826}} enters the {{ill|Kishiwada Domain|fr|Domaine de Kishiwada|ja|岸和田藩|ko|기시와다번|zh|岸和田藩|qid=Q3034469}} of {{ill|Izumi Province|Q1047117|qid=Q1047117}} from the {{ill|Takatsuki Domain|Q10863415|qid=Q10863415}} of {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}} and designates the shrine as the Ichinomiya of the domain.
* {{ill|1737|Q6993|qid=Q6993}} (Genbun 2): Upon petition to the {{ill|Yoshida family|Q11413722|qid=Q11413722|lt=Kyoto Yoshida family}}, the shrine is granted the title “{{ill|Gozu Tennō|de|Gozu-Tennō|it|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|zh|牛頭天王|qid=Q11570247|lt=Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō}}.”
* {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6): Designated as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.
* {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} (Meiji 40): The Suwa Shrine of Kamisuya in {{ill|Amaka|Q11516636|qid=Q11516636}}, {{ill|Sennan District, Osaka|Q1205635|qid=Q1205635}}, is merged into the shrine. Under the directive of the heads of the Shrine and Religion Bureaus of the {{ill|Home Ministry|Q1142265|qid=Q1142265}}, in the so-called “{{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700}},” the deities of Kamisuya and Magami, as well as those of Gokurakuji, Nagaregi, and Hata in {{ill|Habugō|Q11423777|qid=Q11423777}}, were merged. A policy was also proposed to merge them into {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Habiki Shrine}}, located in Habiki of Habiki-gō Village, but opposition led by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamabara Sakutarō}} forced the abandonment of this plan. Although the Hata Hata Shrine was merged, it was later restored as an independent shrine.
* {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} (Meiji 41): Designated as a shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and ritual implements.

=== Origin of the title Ichinomiya ===
Since ancient times, the shrine was known as the Ichinomiya as the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōsha}} of the Amagawa Estate. In the Edo period, when Okabe Nobukatsu entered the Kishiwada Domain from the Takatsuki Domain, there was no Ichinomiya within his territory. In the southern district of the domain, {{ill|Kishiwadahama|Q11475839|qid=Q11475839}}, there was the {{ill|Otabisho|Q11489117|qid=Q11489117}} of the highly ranked {{ill|Tsugawa Shrine|Q11597137|qid=Q11597137}}, which was the Fourth Shrine of Izumi Province, but Tsugawa Village, where Tsugawa Shrine was located, was shogunate land. Therefore, the Otabisho was relocated to Kita-gaku, Komatsuzato Village (territory of the {{ill|Yodo Domain|Q844014|qid=Q844014}} in {{ill|Yamashiro Province|cs|Provincie Jamaširo|de|Provinz Yamashiro|es|Provincia de Yamashiro|fa|ولایت یاماشیرو|fr|Province de Yamashiro|gl|Provincia de Yamashiro|hak|Yamashiro-koet|id|Provinsi Yamashiro|it|Yamashiro (provincia)|ja|山城国|ko|야마시로국|lt|Jamaširo žemė|ms|Yamashiro Province|nl|Yamashiro (provincie)|pt|Província de Yamashiro|ru|Ямасиро (провинция)|simple|Yamashiro Province|sk|Jamaširo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамаширо|tr|Yamashiro (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямашіро|wuu|山城国|zh|山城國|zh_min_nan|Yamasiro-kok|zh_yue|山城國|qid=Q749276}}), which was known for the plaque bestowed by Retired Emperor Shirakawa. At that time, a search was conducted for an old and prestigious shrine within the domain, and Yashirogi Shrine was selected and designated as the Ichinomiya of the Kishiwada Domain. During occasions such as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=daimyō succession}} and {{ill|Sankin-kōtai|Q1151844|qid=Q1151844}}, the domain lord himself would worship here together with {{ill|Senkō-ji Temple|Q17222155|qid=Q17222155}}, the {{ill|Bodaiji|Q1084697|qid=Q1084697}} of the Okabe clan. After the abolition of the domains under the {{ill|Abolition of the han system|Q331905|qid=Q331905}}, the Kishiwada Domain ceased to exist, and the shrine lost its status as the domain’s Ichinomiya, but it is still worshipped by local residents as the Ichinomiya of the Amagawa Valley.

* {{ill|Hata Yashiro no Sukune|Q11555455|qid=Q11555455|lt=Hata Yashiro no Sukune}}
* {{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|qid=Q9150391}} – merged from Kamisuya Shrine ({{ill|Suwa Shrine|Q2370082|qid=Q2370082}})
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} – merged from Magami Shrine ({{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qid=Q11487447}})
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} – merged from Kamisuya Shrine ({{ill|Tenjin Jinja|Q11443287|qid=Q11443287}})
* {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}} – merged from Gokurakuji Shrine ({{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|qid=Q191763}})
* {{ill|Takemikazuchi|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto}} – merged from Nagaregi Shrine ({{ill|Kashima Shrines|Q11677154|qid=Q11677154}})
* Additionally, the Forty-nine Shrine ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ochiai Shrine}}) from Nagaregi Shrine, whose enshrined deity is unknown, has been merged. There is a legend that the heads of forty-nine people who died in battle were buried here.

=== Annual festival ===
During the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sports Day}} holiday in October, the {{ill|Kishiwada Danjiri Festival|Q11475809|qid=Q11475809}} is held, featuring the shrine entry ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miyairi}}) of the Higashi-Kishiwada Danjiri Festival.

A total of five danjiri floats participate from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hatta-chō}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Magami-chō}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamisuyachō}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gokurakuji-chō}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nagaregi-chō}}.

The festival also features the very rare {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=portable shrine procession}}.

The portable shrine procession takes place during the danjiri’s departure from the shrine. The mikoshi is carried by the duty town (the town that enters the shrine last), rotating among the five towns, and the danjiri follow the mikoshi in procession to the {{ill|Otabisho|Q11489117|qid=Q11489117}}.

The Otabisho is located at the former site of Suwa Shrine (Kamisuyachō).

The previous mikoshi was made by {{ill|Kishiki Shrine|Q119929652|qid=Q119929652}}, but it was considered of too low a rank to be carried, so Yashirogi Shrine purchased it.

=== Subordinate shrines ===
* {{ill|Inari shrine|Q514480|qid=Q514480}} – Enshrines {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shirotaka Daimyōjin}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kōryō Daimyōjin}}.
* {{ill|Dōsojin|Q269515|qid=Q269515|lt=Dōso Shrine}} (Ashigami-sama) – It is said that people with foot ailments or pain will be healed by rubbing the stone.
* {{ill|Benzaiten|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaiten}} – Transferred ({{ill|Sengū|Q2271023|qid=Q2271023}}) from Nagaregi Shrine ({{ill|Benzaiten|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaiten Shrine}}).

=== Access ===
From {{ill|Kishiwada Station|Q6416611|qid=Q6416611}} on the {{ill|Nankai Main Line|Q59453|qid=Q59453}} or {{ill|Higashi-Kishiwada Station|Q857440|qid=Q857440}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|Q1154800|qid=Q1154800}}, take the {{ill|Nankai Wing Bus|Q11408142|qid=Q11408142}} routes 641, 642, 643, or 644, get off at the “Ichinomiya” bus stop, then walk south for 3 minutes.

* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Arima Shrine}} – Located in Kubo, Kaizuka City, Osaka Prefecture. A shrine associated with the Amaka clan, powerful families of the Amagawa Estate. It was founded in 507, very close in date to this shrine.
* {{ill|Yukiai-dō Temple|Q17225570|qid=Q17225570}} (Kamisuyachō) – When Shinto rites of the former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amagawa Estate}} were held, the lower districts (Gokurakuji, Hata, Nagaregi) and upper districts (Hatta, Kamisuya, Magami) would meet at this hall and then proceed together to worship at Yashirogi Shrine.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Magami Hachidai Ryūō Shrine}} (Magami-chō) – After an accident in which people collecting earth at the former site of Yasaka Shrine were buried and died, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hachidai Ryūō}} and the {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}} were enshrined here after the war.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kaigan-ji ruins}} (Handa-chō, Kaizuka City) – A temple built by Okabe Nobukatsu of the Kishiwada Domain to memorialize the Tokugawa family. Abolished in Meiji 2. The gravestone of the monk Ien Hōshi Daiku bears the inscription “Amagawa Ichinomiya (Yashirogi Shrine), 11th generation.”
